_meta.what: The one table that knows anything about a specific Apify actor. Research jobs ask for a job by name; this file says which actor does it, what to send, how to read what comes back, and roughly what it costs. Actors are made by independent developers: they get renamed, repriced and reshaped. When one breaks, change its entry here. No Python changes.
_meta.prices: Every price here is an ESTIMATE taken from the actor's public pricing page on the checked date, at the free plan's rate (the most expensive tier, so estimates lean high). Apify can change prices at any time. `factory.py research actors` compares these numbers with the live price for free and says when they have drifted.

fields.actor: the actor's public id, written user/name
fields.purpose: what the job is for, in plain words
fields.inputs_field: the field in the actor's input that receives the person's list (handles, keywords, links)
fields.inputs_as: list = send a JSON list; lines = join into one text value, one entry per line
fields.cap_field: the actor's own input field that limits how much it collects; null means the only limit is how many inputs we send
fields.cap_scope: total = the cap field counts everything in the run; per_input = it counts per handle or keyword, so the client divides the budget
fields.input_template: fixed settings sent on every run. Every paid extra is pinned OFF here on purpose
fields.allowed_inputs: the only extra settings a caller may pass. Anything else is refused, so a typo cannot switch on a paid extra
fields.options: named paid extras a caller must ask for by name, each with its own estimate
fields.output_map: their field -> our field. Dots walk into nested data; [] collects a value from every entry of a list. When two of their fields map to the same one of ours, the first that has a value wins
fields.required_fields: our fields that must appear in at least one result, or the actor's output has changed shape
fields.unit: what one charge buys: result | page | video
fields.est_usd_per_unit: estimated price of one unit, in US dollars
fields.est_usd_per_run: estimated flat fee for starting the actor once
fields.min_ceiling_usd: some actors refuse a spending ceiling below their own minimum; the client never sends less than this
fields.price_event: the name of the actor's main charge, so the live price can be compared
fields.price_addon_events: other charges the fixed settings switch on, added to the live price

creator_instagram.purpose: Recent reels from one or more Instagram accounts: caption, views, likes, comments, length, date.

transcripts.about: A spoken transcript of each reel. Charged per started minute of audio, so a reel over one minute costs more than this estimate. Roughly eighteen times the price of the reel itself.

creator_instagram.notes: Official actor. Input, output and price confirmed from its public listing on the checked date. NOT confirmed: the name of the field the transcript extra writes to (it only appears on paid runs); `transcript` is the best guess. If transcripts come back empty after a paid run, read `their_fields_seen` in that run's record and fix the map here.

creator_tiktok.purpose: Recent videos from one or more TikTok accounts: caption, plays, likes, comments, shares, length, date.
creator_tiktok.notes: Official partner actor. Input, output and price confirmed on the checked date. Its date and popularity filters are paid extras and are deliberately not offered. It gives no transcript text (only links to subtitles TikTok made for some videos), so the spoken hook comes from running the video miner on the few videos worth it. The sibling `tiktok-video-scraper` from the same developer was considered and rejected for this job: it takes single video links, not an account.

creator_youtube_shorts.purpose: Recent Shorts from one or more YouTube channels: title, views, likes, comments, length, date.
creator_youtube_shorts.notes: Same actor as youtube_channel, asked for Shorts only. IMPORTANT for anyone editing this entry: this actor reads a cap of 0 as 'no limit'. The client refuses to send a cap below 1 for exactly this reason.

youtube_search.purpose: What YouTube shows for a keyword right now: titles, channels, views, age, and how big each channel is.
youtube_search.notes: Confirmed on the checked date. Two paid extras are switched ON on purpose because the demand check is meaningless without them: exact publish dates (video stats) and subscriber counts (channel analytics). Together they add a third to the base price, and that is already inside the estimate. A smaller actor (about 140 users), so watch it: if it disappears, any YouTube keyword-search actor that returns views, a publish date and a subscriber count can replace it by editing this entry.

youtube_channel.purpose: A channel's recent long-form videos with views, so each video can be compared with that channel's own normal.
youtube_channel.notes: Confirmed on the checked date. This actor reads a cap of 0 as 'no limit'; the client never sends a cap below 1.

youtube_transcripts.purpose: The words spoken in specific YouTube videos, from the video's own captions.
youtube_transcripts.notes: Confirmed on the checked date. It has no limit setting of its own, so the only cap is how many links are sent: the client trims the list before sending. A video with captions switched off comes back with no transcript; that is normal, not a fault.

reddit_search.purpose: Reddit posts that match a search, in the posters' own words.
reddit_search.notes: Confirmed on the checked date. This actor sells its own paid text analysis (`aiAnalysis`, `customLabels`). Both are pinned OFF and cannot be switched on from here: in the Factory the reading is done by Claude in the conversation, from the saved files. Author names are deliberately not mapped; a quote is cited by its link.

x_search.purpose: Posts on X that match a search, in the posters' own words.
x_search.notes: Confirmed on the checked date. IMPORTANT: left to itself this actor collects up to 100,000 posts per run. A cap is therefore never optional. Author details are deliberately not mapped; a quote is cited by its link.

serp.purpose: What Google shows for a question or keyword: the results, the 'people also ask' questions, and the related searches.
serp.notes: Official actor. Confirmed on the checked date. TWO things to know. (1) It sells a dozen paid extras, several at about 20 cents per query on the free plan, which is over forty times the price of a page. Every one is pinned OFF above and none can be switched on from here. (2) It refuses any spending ceiling under 50 cents, so that is the smallest ceiling the client can send. A normal run still costs a few cents; 50 cents is only the most it could ever charge.
